context: The party is standing in a neglected, low‑light tomb chamber before a weathered statue with a bronze plaque whose inscription is partly obscured by grime, corrosion, or an unfamiliar script; they currently lack a translator or scholar to read it. A passive recognition check determines whether the player identifies the iconography as Jergal, the Scribe of the Dead, or instead offers a tentative, noncommittal guess (e.g., “some kind of scholar” or a forgotten patron). Reading the plaque would normally require Investigation/Religion/language checks and could reveal names, warnings, ritual details, or even trigger environmental effects; the party has arrived here after navigating the tomb’s corridors and hazards. In other branches of the scene, Jergal is a possible later presence (rising from a sarcophagus or appearing at camp) who can interact with the party, but that interaction is separate from the single recognition moment.
